description: Six-panel composite figure mixing SEM and TEM micrographs that tracks how the microstructure of a Ni-containing duplex low-density steel changes with annealing temperature. A left-hand side annotation splits it into a "Micro-scale" block (rows labelled 500 °C and 700 °C) and a "Nano-scale" block (bottom row). (a) SEM image of the 500 °C condition, 50 µm scale bar, with dark elongated regions arrowed as "B2 stringer band" and a lighter matrix arrowed "γ + κ". (b) Higher-magnification SEM of the same condition, 10 µm scale bar, showing a triangular grain outlined by coarse grain-boundary particles arrowed "GB-B2", with the grain interior arrowed "γ + κ". (c) SEM at 700 °C, 50 µm scale bar, again labelled "B2 stringer band" and "γ + κ". (d) 700 °C detail, 4 µm scale bar, with a vertically lettered "B2 stringer band" and a finely precipitate-decorated "γ + κ" matrix. (e) TEM bright-field image, 1 µm scale bar, of dark disc-shaped precipitates arrowed "Nano-disk B2" in the α matrix. (f) TEM bright-field image, 0.2 µm scale bar, labelled "γ + cuboid κ" but with very low contrast, so the cuboid particles are only faintly discernible. Together the panels argue that B2 stringers and grain-boundary B2 dominate at 500–700 °C, while nano-disc B2 and cuboid κ appear at nano-scale.
measured_quantities: phase/precipitate morphology scale (µm, from scale bars)

observations.observation: Panels (a) and (c) are SEM micrographs with identical printed labels, "B2 stringer band" and "γ + κ", and identical 50 µm scale bars, for the 500 °C and 700 °C conditions respectively.
Panel (b) prints the label "GB-B2" pointing at coarse particles along a grain boundary, together with a "γ + κ" label for the grain interior, at a 10 µm scale bar.
Panel (e) prints the label "Nano-disk B2" pointing at dark disc-shaped precipitates dispersed in the matrix, with a 1 µm scale bar, indicating nano-scale B2 discs.
Panel (f) prints the label "γ + cuboid κ" with a 0.2 µm scale bar; the cuboid κ particles themselves are very faint and their size/shape cannot be measured from the supplied image.

The figure prints no quantitative values other than scale-bar lengths (50, 10, 50, 4, 1 and 0.2 µm) and the row temperatures 500 °C and 700 °C; no particle size or composition numbers are printed on any panel.
The caption states that (a) shows nano-sized κ-carbides formed in the interior of γ grains and the formation of B2 stringer bands (initially α phase).
The caption states that (b) shows the formation of coarse grain boundary B2 particles (GB-B2).
The caption states that (c) and (d) show a microstructure similar to that formed during annealing at 500 °C, observed after isothermal holding at 700 °C.

The caption states that (e) is a TEM bright-field image of a disk-like B2 particle in the α matrix after annealing at higher temperatures, e.g. 900 °C and 1050 °C — temperatures that are not printed anywhere on the panels themselves.
The caption states that (f) is a TEM bright-field image of cuboid κ particles in the γ matrix, and that all micrographs show the microstructure of the Ni-containing sample.

The caption states that the Ni-free steel followed a similar trend except at lower annealing temperatures (e.g. 500 °C and 700 °C), where α + needle-like κ-carbides were observed instead of B2 stringer bands.

The citing text states that B2 formed as micron-sized particles and grain-boundary precipitates in the austenite phase and as nano-sized discs in the ferrite between 900 and 1050 °C (referred to as Fig. 2b and e).
The citing text states that the B2 discs were of Ni-Al type in the Ni-containing samples but of Fe-Al type in the Ni-free samples.

The citing text states that from 500 to 700 °C κ-carbides formed nano-sized blocks in the austenite phase in both grades and as micron-sized needles within the ferrite only in the Ni-free sample (Fig. 2b and f).

The citing text states that at low annealing temperature between 500 and 700 °C the ferrite phase in the 5% Ni sample was replaced by B2 stringer bands, matching the stringer bands labelled in (a), (c) and (d).

subfigures.description: Micro-scale SEM micrograph of the sample annealed at 500 °C, 50 µm scale bar. Dark, elongated/stringer features are arrowed "B2 stringer band"; the surrounding lighter matrix is arrowed "γ + κ". Elongated prior-α bands alternate with equiaxed darker γ grains.

Higher-magnification SEM micrograph at 500 °C, 10 µm scale bar. A roughly triangular grain (interior arrowed "γ + κ") is outlined by discontinuous coarse particles along its boundary, arrowed "GB-B2"; a small dark region sits at the upper-left corner.

Micro-scale SEM micrograph after isothermal holding at 700 °C, 50 µm scale bar, with the same labelling scheme as (a): dark "B2 stringer band" regions in a lighter "γ + κ" matrix. Morphology closely resembles the 500 °C condition.

Higher-magnification SEM micrograph at 700 °C, 4 µm scale bar. A vertically lettered "B2 stringer band" separates regions of finely precipitate-decorated matrix labelled "γ + κ"; dark unresolved particles are embedded in the band.

TEM bright-field image, 1 µm scale bar, of the α matrix containing numerous dark, rounded disc-shaped precipitates arrowed "Nano-disk B2" (typically a few tens of nm across), dispersed fairly uniformly with some slight clustering.

TEM bright-field image, 0.2 µm scale bar, labelled "γ + cuboid κ". Contrast is very low; only faint cuboid/rectangular particle shapes and a weak cross-hatched fringe pattern are discernible in the γ matrix.

unreadable_items: panel (f): contrast is very low — cuboid κ particle size, spacing and shape are only faintly visible and cannot be measured
panel (d): the fine precipitates inside the γ + κ matrix are below the resolution of the supplied image and cannot be individually resolved
panels (a), (c): the nano-sized interior precipitates stated in the caption to be κ-carbides are not resolvable at the 50 µm scale-bar magnification
